trace.code: Cleanup(refresh_sv);   // releases sv_ -> may free cfd_
void ForwardIterator::SVCleanup(DBImpl* db, SuperVersion* sv, ...) { if (sv->Unref()) { ... sv->Cleanup(); ... delete sv; } }

preconditions: The embedding application opens a TAILING iterator (ReadOptions::tailing=true) with an iterate_upper_bound on a column family.
The application then drops that column family and destroys its ColumnFamilyHandle while the iterator is still open — a lifecycle pattern RocksDB did not defend against (fix #15704 adds the defense).
A seek past the largest key of an L0 file trims a child iterator (has_iter_trimmed_for_upper_bound_ = true), so the next SeekToFirst()/backward Seek() calls RebuildIterators(true).

evidence.vulnerable_version: every release through v11.13.2 (tagged 2026-10-28); the fix dec85e6 merged 2026-11-17 is not an ancestor of any release tag
evidence.fixed_version: unreleased (main only; dec85e6 is not in v11.13.2 or any earlier tag)
evidence.observed_result: poc.cc transcribes the verbatim vulnerable/fixed RebuildIterators ordering and the ColumnFamilyData/SuperVersion reference-counting, driven against a deterministic arena that poisons freed blocks. Vulnerable path: Cleanup(true) -> SVCleanup -> sv_->Unref() destroys the SuperVersion, releasing the last ColumnFamilyData reference (refs 1 -> 0, CFD deleted+poisoned); the next line cfd_->GetReferencedSuperVersion() reads the freed CFD and returns a SuperVersion with version_number_ = 0xdededededededede. Heap reuse then shows the dangling cfd_ aliasing a newly allocated 'EVIL_CFD' object (type confusion). The fixed path (dec85e6) keeps sv_ because it is still current, never frees the CFD, and reads version_number_ = 7. Markers: ROCKSGHOST-UAF-CONFIRMED / ROCKSGHOST-TYPE-CONFUSION (vulnerable) vs ROCKSGHOST-NO-UAF (fixed).

real_exploit.target: meta/rocksdb — db/forward_iterator.cc ForwardIterator::RebuildIterators / Cleanup / SVCleanup (vulnerable @ f16beed5 / v11.13.2) and the fixed RebuildIterators @ dec85e6, plus the ColumnFamilyData/SuperVersion reference-counting semantics documented in the fix's own root-cause analysis
real_exploit.backend: a faithful C++ transcription of the exact vulnerable/fixed reference-counting lifetime graph (ColumnFamilyData::Ref/UnrefAndTryDelete, SuperVersion::Ref/Unref/Cleanup holding the last CFD reference, ForwardIterator holding a raw cfd_ + an owning sv_), compiled with zig cc and run against a deterministic arena that poisons freed blocks and reuses them LIFO — turning the ASan-reported heap-use-after-free into an observable, deterministic differential (vulnerable vs fixed)
real_exploit.demonstrated: The vulnerable RebuildIterators(true) frees the ColumnFamilyData through the SuperVersion teardown, then dereferences the dangling cfd_ pointer: the rebuilt SuperVersion's version_number_ reads 0xdededededededede from the poisoned freed block, and a subsequent ColumnFamilyData allocation (heap reuse) makes the dangling cfd_ alias an attacker-reused object (name_ = EVIL_CFD, version 0x7777) — the classic use-after-free -> type-confusion consequence. The fixed RebuildIterators keeps sv_ (it is still the current SuperVersion), never frees the CFD, and reads the correct version 7.

notes: 0-day in the current release line: the fix dec85e6 (2026-11-17) is not an ancestor of v11.13.2 (tagged 2026-10-28) or any earlier tag. CWE-416 use-after-free, ASan-confirmed by the RocksDB fix's root-cause analysis (ColumnFamilyData::GetThreadLocalSuperVersion). Honest severity MEDIUM 6.2: the trigger requires the embedding application to drop a column family while a tailing iterator with an upper bound is still open (an API-lifecycle pattern RocksDB previously did not defend against), and full RCE is not demonstrated — the demonstrated effect is the deterministic dangling-pointer read + heap-reuse type confusion.
